Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the chase to begin. The pair of Ines McKeon and Kate Pelle walks out as the openers for Australia Women Under-19. For Scotland Women Under-19, Mollie Parker will bowl the very first over of the chase.
... The Run Chase ...

The Australian bowlers delivered a masterclass performance, showcasing exceptional discipline and control throughout the game. With a focus on accuracy and targeting the stumps, they successfully restricted the Scottish batters. The wicket-takers for Australia were Eleanor Larosa and Caoimhe Bray, who both claimed three wickets each, while Hasrat Gill took two. Tegan Williamson and Juliette Morton chipped in with one wicket apiece, rounding out a dominant bowling display.

The Scotland Women Under-19 batting innings was stifled from the outset, with wickets falling regularly at the top and the Australian bowlers maintaining a tight grip, never allowing the Scots to build any meaningful partnerships. Only Emma Walsingham and Charlotte Nevard managed to reach double figures, highlighting the struggles of the Scottish batters against a high-quality opponent. The highest partnership of just 19 runs further emphasizes the dominance of the Australian bowlers.
Australia Women Under-19 have made a stellar start to their campaign, dismantling the Scottish batting lineup and limiting them to a modest total of just 48 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for the ICC Under-19 Women's T20 World Cup 2025 match! The umpires have taken their positions in the middle, and the Australian team, captained by Eleanor Larosa, has entered the field, ready to take on Scotland. We're just moments away from the first delivery. The openers for Scotland Women Under-19 are Pippa Kelly and Emma Walsingham. For Australia Women Under-19, Chloe Ainsworth will bowl the first over of this contest.

A moment of great pride and patriotism is unfolding! The Scotland Women Under-19 and Australia Women Under-19 teams have taken to the field, standing united in respect as they prepare to play their national anthems. It will begin with the Scottish national anthem, followed by the Australian national anthem.

Kate Pelle of Australia Women Under-19 is up for a quick chat and she says that the group is a lot more experienced and they're all pumped up for this. Mentions that most of the players have been in those domestic leagues and that will give them a massive edge in terms of performing in those pressure situations.

Skipper of Scotland Women Under-19, Niamh Muir says how they will emerge from those pressure situations will be the key. Mentions that the team is pumped up for such a tournament and they've had a good prep coming into this.

Skipper of Australia Women Under-19, Lucy Hamilton says they are looking to bowl as this a new track and they're not sure how it'll play out. Mentions that they have a lot of preparations building up to it with a few games under their belt.

Australia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Kate Pelle, Ines McKeon, Lucy Hamilton, Caoimhe Bray, Eleanor Larosa (C), Hasrat Gill, Chloe Ainsworth, Grace Lyons (WK), Tegan Williamson, Juliette Morton, Amy Hunter.

Scotland Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Pippa Kelly, Emma Walsingham, Pippa Sproul(WK), Niamh Muir(C), Nayma Sheikh, Charlotte Nevard, Ammy Baldie, Maisie Maceira, Mollie Parker, Kirsty McColl, Lucy Forrester Smith.
TOSS - Australia Women Under-19 have won the toss and they have decided to BOWL first.

The stage is set for an exciting opening day, with six matches in total, and the anticipation is palpable. Will Australia assert their dominance, or will Scotland surprise everyone with a strong performance? Join us in celebrating the future of women’s cricket as these young athletes take their first steps on the world stage! Stay tuned for the toss and the team news...

As we look back at the inaugural edition held in South Africa, India made history by becoming the first Women's Under-19 World Champions. With the format featuring four groups of four teams, followed by Super Sixes and knockout rounds, every match is crucial, providing ample opportunities for teams to shine. Both Australia and Scotland are returning from the last tournament, with Australia aiming to reclaim their status and Scotland eager to prove their growth as a competitive cricketing nation.

Welcome to the highly anticipated second edition of the Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup, where the excitement of cricket takes center stage in Malaysia! With 16 teams competing for glory, this tournament promises to showcase the incredible talent and potential of young female cricketers from around the globe. The opening match features an exhilarating clash between Australia Women Under-19 and Scotland Women Under-19 at the YSD-UKM Cricket Oval in Bangi, setting the tone for what is sure to be an unforgettable tournament.
... MATCHDAY ...

Cricket as a global game has surpassed many barriers and has grown leaps and bounds in recent years and the Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup is a testament to that. The second edition of the T20 global extravaganza will take place in Malaysia and will feature as many as 16 teams who will have a chance to showcase their budding talent on the global stage. In the opening contest at the YSD-UKM Cricket Oval in Bangi, it will be Australia Women Under-19 taking on Scotland Women Under-19 in an enticing contest and there will be as many as 6 games played on Day 1 of the competition. Let's recap what happened in the inaugural edition of the competition that took place in South Africa a couple of years ago. The original event was supposed to take place in 2021 but was delayed and it was the Indian side that reigned supreme, making history as the first Women's Under-19 World Champions. The second edition is slated to be bigger and better, featuring even more talent and this is where we get a peak into the future of women's cricket on the whole. 16 teams divided into 4 groups of four teams followed by two groups of 6 teams and then the Super Sixes before finally moving on to the semi-finals and final, which means loads of opportunities for every team to make a mark. Talking about the teams, both Australia Women Under-19 and Scotland Women Under-19 featured in the inaugural edition with the former bowing out in the semis against arch-rivals England and the latter losing all three group matches. But, things could be well different this time around, especially for Scotland Women Under-19 who as a women's cricketing nation have grown a lot and with the senior team making big strides, they will be expected to push the bigger teams to the limit here. As for Australia Women Under-19, they will be itching to follow in the footsteps of their men counterparts who are the reigning Under-19 champions as well and would want a place in the Final, at the very least. Who do you think will kick off the competition with the win?
